Package com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest

Class BarColumnChecks

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest.BarColumnChecks
public final class BarColumnChecks extends Object
Bar support and collapse in a live level that does not touch loader-native automation directly: item validity, grounding at the bottom of a column, footprint overlap deciding support across the alternating layer orientations, and player extraction dropping what it unsupports. Loader-native automation and protection-event tests stay in each loader's GameTest classes.

  • Method Details

    • validityAndBottomGroundingAreEnforced

      public static void validityAndBottomGroundingAreEnforced(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Bar accepts configured ingots on its grounded bottom layer and rejects other items or unsupported positions. To reproduce in-game: deposit a configured ingot into a bottom Bar position, then try a non-ingot and a floating position. Only the grounded ingot is stored.

    • upperBarRequiresOverlappingSupport

      public static void upperBarRequiresOverlappingSupport(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A Bar above the bottom layer needs footprint overlap with a Bar beneath it. To reproduce in-game: place one bottom Bar, then try depositing above both an overlapping and a disjoint position. Only the overlapping Bar remains.

    • playerExtractionDropsUnsupportedBars

      public static void playerExtractionDropsUnsupportedBars(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Player extraction cascades through Bars that lose support. To reproduce in-game: build a vertical chain of supported Bars and extract its bottom Bar. The unsupported Bars above drop.

    • supportedNeighborSurvivesPlayerExtraction

      public static void supportedNeighborSurvivesPlayerExtraction(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A neighboring Bar with another overlapping support survives a player cascade. To reproduce in-game: support an upper Bar with two lower Bars, then extract one lower support. The upper Bar remains on the other.

    • differentlyOrientedSeamUsesFootprintOverlap

      public static void differentlyOrientedSeamUsesFootprintOverlap(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Bar support across a block seam follows cuboid footprint overlap between alternating layers. To reproduce in-game: fill a top-layer Bar below, then deposit into an overlapping bottom position of the Bar block above. The cross-oriented overlap supports it.

    • depositTraceStopsAtLastEmptyBeforeOccupiedBar

      public static void depositTraceStopsAtLastEmptyBeforeOccupiedBar(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A Bar deposit ray selects the last empty bar before the first occupied bar. To reproduce in-game: place a Bar in the farther position of a bottom-layer row and aim through the empty nearer position. The new Bar occupies the nearer position rather than passing through it.

    • breakingLowerBlockCollapsesDependentUpperBlock

      public static void breakingLowerBlockCollapsesDependentUpperBlock(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Breaking a lower Bar block collapses Bars in the block above that depended on its seam. To reproduce in-game: build supported Bars across a two-block seam and break the lower block. The upper dependent Bars drop and its empty block disappears.

    • breakingFullColumnConsolidatesDrops

      public static void breakingFullColumnConsolidatesDrops(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Breaking a full Bar column drops all contents without spawning one entity per Bar. To reproduce in-game: fill a Bar block with one ingot type and break it. Every ingot is returned in consolidated dropped stacks.

    • playerCascadeConsolidatesAcrossBlocks

      public static void playerCascadeConsolidatesAcrossBlocks(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A player-triggered cascade consolidates matching drops across block boundaries. To reproduce in-game: build a dense supported Bar column spanning two blocks and remove its lowest support. All unsupported Bars are returned in consolidated item entities.

    • collapseDoesNotMergeDifferentComponents

      public static void collapseDoesNotMergeDifferentComponents(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A Bar collapse never merges stacks with different data components. To reproduce in-game: build a supported Bar chain from otherwise identical items carrying distinct components, then remove the support. Each component identity remains a separate drop.

    • comparatorReservesZeroForAnEmptyColumn

      public static void comparatorReservesZeroForAnEmptyColumn(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The comparator range reserves 0 for an empty column, as a vanilla container's does, and a position holds one bar, so full means every position of every block occupied.

      To reproduce in-game: compare an empty Bar column, the same column with one Bar, and a full column. Their comparator outputs are 0, at least 1, and 15 respectively.

    • comparatorReadsTheWholeColumnFromEveryBlock

      public static void comparatorReadsTheWholeColumnFromEveryBlock(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Every block in a Bar column reports the same whole-column fill. To reproduce in-game: make a two-block column with one block full and the other empty, then place comparators against both. Their outputs match.

    • comparatorFollowsAColumnLosingABlock

      public static void comparatorFollowsAColumnLosingABlock(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The fill is measured against the column's current height, so a run that loses a block reports the same contents as a larger share of a smaller column.

      To reproduce in-game: fill the lower half of a two-block Bar column, read its comparator, then remove the empty upper block. The lower block's output rises from half full to full.
